campaign.name: Premium grain-free, vet-formulated dog food for senior dogs, sold by subscription · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $70 first order (assumed) × 0.60 = $42.00 target CPA: subscription revenue repeats, so a first order can be bought at a larger share of its value. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

test_plan.hypothesis: Every shopper here is a dog owner already comfortable with a recurring pet box, so a food subscription is a natural next step; the open question is how many of these 25-45 'millennials treating dogs as family' actually have a senior dog, and whether a vet-formulated pitch lands where a 'fun, playful brand voice converts best'.
test_plan.risk: Young owner skew means few senior dogs, and a $70 first order is double the $35 typical basket, so the clinical/premium message may under-convert against this playful audience.
test_plan.promote_if: CPA at or below the $42.00 target after 14 days: move it to core.
test_plan.cut_if: CPA above the $54.60 maximum, or no conversions after 14 days: stop it.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

launch_summary.summary: The entire $10,000 budget sits on one test placement, Tailcrate, where shoppers are proven dog owners already buying a pet subscription; the two large pet-food publishers are competitors and every non-pet publisher was excluded for having no dog-related purchase moment. The test asks how many of Tailcrate's younger, playful-voiced audience actually own a senior dog, and whether a vet-formulated pitch converts there. Four ads run for The Pet Parent, The Busy Parent, The Wellness Optimizer and The Convenience-First Millennial, with Tailcrate promoted to core if cost per new customer lands at or below $42.00 after 14 days.
uncertainties: The $70 first order value is assumed, and both the $42.00 target and $54.60 maximum cost per new customer are built on it.
No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so all results are exploratory rather than a proven base to scale from.
Tailcrate's shoppers skew 25-45 with a $35 typical basket, so there may be few senior dogs and resistance to a $70 first order.
questions: What is your actual first order price and margin, so the target cost per new customer can be corrected?
How long does a typical subscriber stay, so we can judge what a first order is worth?
Do you sell any one-time purchase option, or is subscription genuinely the only way to buy?
